submitted.rationale: Out of 3 merit measurements, 24 (Bi0.088 Cu0.466 V0.446) had the highest photocurrent, 49.6 µA. This is the copper-vanadate region near Cu2V2O7, which has a visible-light gap. The neighbouring point 119 gave 43 µA, which confirms this is a productive region. The BiVO4-side point 143 gave 22.9 µA.

rejected.reason: BiVO4-like composition with about 21% Cu measured 22.9 µA, less than half of 24.
More Cu-rich neighbour of 24; measured 43 µA, slightly lower.
Not measured. MEGNet predicts a 0.32 eV gap for CuO, so CuO-dominated films are likely to recombine carriers rather than act as photoanodes.

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE gaps: V2O5 2.83 eV (near/above 2.72 eV photon energy), Cu2O 1.56 eV. Weak support: the model results don't speak to BiVO4 directly (ID lookup failed). Measuring 143 (Bi0.36 Cu0.21 V0.43) because it sits near the BiVO4 Bi:V≈1 line, a known visible-light photoanode, and has the least Cu. It is the region's prior-knowledge anchor.

MEGNet HSE gives CuO 0.32 eV, a narrow-gap absorber that would likely act as a recombination/dark phase. That argues against the Cu-rich corner (Cu>0.7). Measuring 24 (Cu≈V, Bi 0.09) to test the copper-vanadate (Cu2V2O7-type, ~2 eV gap) photoanode region instead. This is a contrast point against the BiVO4-side result.

MEGNet HSE gives Bi2O3 2.34 eV. This does not directly concern the Cu-V region: Bi oxide absorbs at 2.72 eV but is not a strong photoanode by itself, so adding more Bi gains little. Supports keeping Bi low. Measuring 119 (Bi 0.08, Cu 0.50, V 0.42): it sits next to the best point so far (24, 49.6 µA), closer to Cu2V2O7 stoichiometry, with less Bi.
